doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Quincy Jones, Chick Corea, Joe Farrell and Sam Noto
summary: Funk Junction on Vanguard, sitting in with Corea, and an album with Sam Noto at Donte's.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Let me ask you about a couple of people here that you’ve played for or with or they’ve played with you. Quincy Jones?
Oh yeah. Quincy I actually did a recording for John Hammond on Vanguard and Quincy wrote one of the tunes, called “Funk Junction.” That was before he became very popular as a writer.
Chick Corea, I just sat in with Chick when he was out here and went over to his house at a Valentine’s Day party or something, and played a little bit.
He’s always liked jazz flute, hasn’t he?
Right. And of course we made that record with Joe Farrell, one of his flutists, but then he died.
Yeah. That was a shame. I know you’ve recorded with, oh Sam Noto, look at that.
Sam Noto is on one of the Xanadu albums, right? Have you heard some of these?
Yes. And I met Sam, yeah.
Oh, okay, so he was out here and we did a thing at Donte’s, we did an album together with Sam, Sam Noto.
